structure: Part 1, Live-animals journey routes. Read in full: src/k6/journeys.js (552 lines, the shared notification walker: dashboard, create, draft sessions, review and declaration, read-back, amend, cancel-amend, backend replay), src/k6/live-animals.js (232 lines, the 13 live-animals draft steps, the re-edit list and the amend edit), src/k6/journey-pages.js (167 lines, page path, save check, choice and address-picker helpers), src/k6/documents.js (146 lines, the accompanying-documents upload, status poll and continue), src/k6/pages.js (172 lines, the walker that opens, posts, submits, uploads and reaches pages), src/config/journey-endpoints.js (103 lines, the endpoint tags per step and the shared-page tags), src/config/smoke.js (112 lines, JOURNEYS set bases, identity and scenarios), src/config/test-data.js (73 lines, commodity search, document date and scan timing), src/lib/redirects.js (120 lines, create-path id parsing, staleAction and sign-in hop rules), src/lib/forms.js (52 lines), src/lib/form-fill.js (111 lines, blank-field answer rules and the d/m/yyyy date writer), src/lib/redirects.test.js (154 lines, read only to confirm routes and the draft id shape) and the workspace page docs/repos/trade-imports-performance-tests.md (134 lines, context). There is no route table: routes appear as the set base '/live-animals', the create path '<setBase>/notifications', the notification base '<setBase>/notifications/<id>' and the page slugs each step opens under it. Covered: the journey dashboard at the set root and its search by ?referenceNumber=, the create POST and the id read from its redirect, the hub at the notification base, all 13 live-animals steps in STEP_ENDPOINTS order (origin, commodities with search, consignment-details, commodities/identification, import-reason, additional-details, accompanying-documents with upload and status, addresses with five party pickers and their search, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries with add, transporters, consignment/contact/select) with every field name and value posted, the re-edit list, notification-view, declaration and its save, confirmation, amend, cancel-amend and its save, the three backend requests (fulfilments, list by referenceNumber, replace), the staleAction and sign-in redirect rules, and every check name the scripts make. The scripts assert no page heading, caption or copy: their only text check is that the dashboard search page contains the reference number. Left to part 2: the INS front door (sign-in pages, INS dashboard, address book). Left out by the partition: the high-risk plants journey and harness internals (think time, traffic classes, metrics, redirect-hop limits, eventing). The suite has no germinal-products journey anywhere under src/.

claims.statement: The live-animals journey's set base is the path /live-animals.
The live-animals journey is served by trade-imports-animals-frontend.
The live-animals journey persists its notifications in trade-imports-animals-backend.
Live animals has a single notification type, 'live-animals', unlike high-risk plants which splits by commodity type.
claims.quote:
Live animals has one type. High-risk plants has one per commodity type in
 * the traffic model.

claims.statement: Opening the set root /live-animals renders the live-animals journey dashboard, and that page carries a non-empty crumb (form token) a user posts back to create a notification.
claims.quote:
'journey dashboard opens with a crumb': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK && page.crumb !== ''
claims.note: The partition names this set-root dashboard as the request inc-129 stops serving when the notification list moves to the INS front door; that is context from the partition, not something this repo says.

claims.statement: Each journey session signs in through the INS front door and opens the INS dashboard before it opens the live-animals journey dashboard.
claims.note: The INS front door itself is part 2's to claim.

claims.statement: A new live-animals notification is created by posting the dashboard's crumb to the create path /live-animals/notifications.
Creating a live-animals draft redirects to /live-animals/notifications/<id>/origin, so origin is the first page a new draft lands on.
claims.quote:
'draft created through the frontend': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK &&
      id !== '' &&
      page.url.endsWith(`/${run.journey.firstSavePage}`)

claims.statement: The notification id is the path segment straight after the create path in the URL the create request redirects to.
claims.quote: Reads the notification id from the URL a create request redirects to.

claims.statement: A draft notification id looks like DRAFT.GB.2026.1, per the unit test of the id parser.
claims.note: Test fixture value; it shows the shape the suite expects, not a format the frontend is proven to issue.

claims.statement: Each notification's pages sit under the notification base /live-animals/notifications/<id>, at <base>/<slug>.
The notification base itself (/live-animals/notifications/<id>) is the notification hub page.
A draft can be drafted across more than one session: a later session signs in afresh and continues the same draft by opening its hub.
claims.quote:
Runs one notification as a real user would: drafted across one or two
 * sessions, submitted, read back, then amended and cancelled or resubmitted.

claims.statement: The live-animals draft steps, in order, are: origin, commodities, consignment-details, identification, import-reason, additional-details, documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, contact.
Every step save is expected to land on a page that renders, with no redirect loop and no staleAction redirect; a step whose save lands otherwise fails its '<step> saved' check.
The origin page is at <base>/origin.
The origin page has a countryOfOrigin select whose options the suite draws from at random, falling back to FR.
The origin page has a regionOfOriginCodeRequirement field, answered 'no'.
The origin page has an internalReferenceNumber text field, answered with a value of the form PERF-<vu>-<iteration>, plus -A when amending.
The commodities page is at <base>/commodities and has a commodity search box named commoditySearch, submitted with action=search.
The suite searches commodities for 'Cow'.
The live-animals step list depends on the commodity chosen: only Cow's pages match the step list the suite walks exactly, so other commodities bring different pages.
claims.quote: // Cow is the one commodity whose pages match the live-animals step list exactly.
claims.note: That other commodities change the pages follows from 'the one commodity whose pages match'; the comment does not say which pages differ.

claims.statement: The commodity search results offer species choices named species, and saving one of them saves the commodities page.
The consignment-details page is at <base>/consignment-details, and every blank text field and unselected select on it is answered.
claims.note: The suite names no consignment-details field; it fills whatever blank fields the page renders.

claims.statement: The identification page is at <base>/commodities/identification, and every blank text field and unselected select on it is answered.

Blank fields are answered by name: a field starting numberOfAnimalsQuantity gets 1, numberOfPackages gets 5, a name containing 'tag' gets UK123456789012, 'quantity' gets 5, otherwise PERF<vu><iteration>; these values pass the animals pages' validation.
claims.note: commodityCode, eppoCode and species rules in the same table are plants values and not claimed here.

claims.statement: An unselected select is answered with its first non-empty option, so selects open on an empty placeholder option.
claims.quote: Picks the first option that is not the empty placeholder.
claims.note: That the pages' selects start on an empty placeholder is read from the helper skipping one.

claims.statement: Search boxes named q, commoditySearch, search or referenceNumber are never filled as answers.
The import-reason page is at <base>/import-reason, with a reasonForImport field answered 'internalMarket'.
The import-reason page has a purposeInInternalMarket field, answered 'breeding' when the reason is internal market.
The additional-details page is at <base>/additional-details, with an animalsCertifiedFor choice that has an option labelled 'Slaughter'.
The additional-details page has a containsUnweanedAnimals choice that has an option labelled 'No'.
Radio and checkbox choices on the journey pages each have a label tied to the input by its id, which is how the suite finds a choice by its label text.
claims.note: Read from the helper's lookup; the suite falls back to the first choice when no label matches.

claims.statement: The documents page is at <base>/accompanying-documents.
A document is added on the documents page with a multipart upload of one file plus accompanyingDocumentReference, accompanyingDocumentType, accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue and action=add.
claims.quote:
accompanyingDocumentReference: reference,
  accompanyingDocumentType: pickFrom(
    context,
    selectOptions(page.formInputs, 'accompanyingDocumentType')
  ),

claims.statement: accompanyingDocumentType is a select whose options the suite draws from at random.
The backend accepts a document reference of letters and digits only.
claims.quote: // The backend accepts a document reference of letters and digits only.

claims.statement: The document date of issue is entered as one text field in d/m/yyyy, here 30 days before today.
Date fields on the journey pages take a single text value written d/m/yyyy with no zero padding, the way the frontends render a date.
claims.quote: Writes a date the way the frontends render one, in UTC.

claims.statement: A successful document upload lands back on <base>/accompanying-documents.
Uploaded documents go through the frontend to the real cdp-uploader and its virus scan.
claims.quote:
Each document goes through the frontend to the real cdp-uploader and its
 * virus scan.

claims.statement: The documents page has a JSON status route at <base>/accompanying-documents/status listing the documents and their scan state, which the page's script polls every 3 seconds until nothing is pending.
claims.quote:
The step then polls the frontend's status route, as the page's
 * script does every 3 seconds, until nothing is pending

claims.statement: A document scan that stays pending for more than 120 seconds is treated as stuck.
A scanned document must settle and must not be rejected by the scan.
claims.quote:
'document scan settled': isScanned,
    'document scan not rejected': (listed) => !scanWasRejected(listed)

claims.statement: The document scan is held to a P99 under 60 seconds, the same allowance as upload pages.
claims.quote: 'Document scan allowance: P99 under 60s, as for upload pages (DR-EUDP-005 section 4.7, SYN-28, SYN-29)'

claims.statement: The documents page is left by submitting action=continue; with no documents to add, the page is only opened and continued.
The addresses page is at <base>/addresses.

From the addresses page five party pickers are filled in order: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, destination, at <base>/place-of-origin/select, consignors/select, consignees/select, importers/select and destinations/select.
Each party picker has a search box named q, submitted with action=search, and lists matching addresses as radios named party, saved with action=save.
Saving a picker lands back on the page it came from.
claims.quote: The picker's own save lands on the page it came from.

claims.statement: A picker search must answer a 255-character search term, the longest an address-book name may be.
claims.quote:
// The longest searchable address field: ins-frontend features/address-book/fields.js FIELD_RULES.name.maxLength.
export const WORST_CASE_SEARCH_LENGTH = 255

claims.statement: The pickers search for and choose the performance-test address named 'Perf Test Holding', 4 Nursery Lane, Perth, PH1 5EX.
claims.quote:
name: 'Perf Test Holding',
  addressLine1: '4 Nursery Lane',
claims.note: The wiring of PERF_ADDRESS.name into addressName is in src/suites/, outside this part's read; the pickers search by addressName.

claims.statement: After the five pickers, the addresses page is reopened and saved with an empty form.
The CPH number page is at <base>/cph-number and takes the CPH as three fields: cphCounty (12), cphParish (345) and cphHolding (6789).
The port-of-entry page is at <base>/port-of-entry, with an arrivalDateAtPort date field answered 7 days ahead.
The port-of-entry page has a portOfEntry select drawn at random from its options, falling back to 'GB ABD'.
The port-of-entry page has a meansOfTransport field, answered 'ROAD_VEHICLE'.
The port-of-entry page has a transportIdentification field, answered 'FR-892-LK'.
The port-of-entry page has a transportDocumentReference field, answered 'CMR-2026-884721'.
The transit-countries page is at <base>/transit-countries and adds a country by posting a transitedCountry select value with action=add, falling back to FR.
claims.quote:
transitedCountry: drawnOrElse(
          context,
          opened.formInputs,
          'transitedCountry',
          FRANCE
        ),
        action: 'add'

claims.statement: After a transit country is added, the transit-countries page is saved with an empty form.
The transporters page is at <base>/transporters and offers transporter radios named transporter, saved with action=save.
The contact step is at <base>/consignment/contact/select and offers address radios named contactAddress, from which the performance-test address is chosen by its label.
claims.quote:
'consignment/contact/select',
  ENDPOINTS.contact,
  ({ addressName }, page) => ({
    contactAddress: choiceLabelled(page, 'contactAddress', addressName)

claims.statement: After the draft steps, origin, import-reason, additional-details, cph-number and port-of-entry are reopened and saved again before submission, so answered pages can be revisited and resaved.
Submission starts at the notification-view page, <base>/notification-view.
The declaration page is at <base>/declaration and is submitted with declaration=confirmed.
Submitting the declaration lands on a URL ending /confirmation.
claims.note: Check name 'submitted through the declaration page' for a first submission.

claims.statement: The live-animals dashboard can be searched by reference number with /live-animals?referenceNumber=<id>.
A submitted notification appears on the dashboard search results: the page text contains its reference number.
claims.quote:
'submitted notification is on the dashboard': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK && page.html.text().includes(run.id)

claims.statement: After submission the hub and the notification-view page both still open.
claims.quote: check(hub, { 'submitted hub reads back': (page) => page.status === HTTP_OK })

claims.statement: A submitted notification is amended by posting the crumb to <base>/amend, which lands on the hub at <base>.
claims.note: The crumb comes from the dashboard search page.

claims.statement: The amendment edits the origin page.
An amendment can be cancelled from <base>/cancel-amend by submitting its form, which lands on notification-view with cancelled=1 in the URL.
An amendment not cancelled is resubmitted through notification-view and the declaration, landing on /confirmation.
The animals backend serves a notification's fulfilments at GET /notifications/<id>/fulfilments.
The animals backend lists notifications by reference number at GET /notifications?referenceNumber=<id>, returning them under content.
The animals backend replaces a notification with PUT /notifications/<id> and a JSON body built from the fulfilments and list reads, answering 200.
claims.quote:
'backend replay accepted the captured save': (response) =>
      response.status === HTTP_OK

claims.statement: When a save is out of date the journey redirects the user back with staleAction=1 in the URL, for example /live-animals?staleAction=1.
claims.quote: The journey sends the user back with `staleAction=1` when a save is out of date.
claims.note: That the redirect goes to the set root is only shown by test fixtures.

claims.statement: Sign-in passes through the frontend's /auth routes and the identity provider (/oauth2/, /idphub/, /organisations), ending at the OIDC callback /oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote:
Every hop through the frontend's `/auth` routes and the identity provider
 * counts as `sign-in`.

claims.statement: Opening the live-animals dashboard while signed out can redirect through sign-in before reaching /live-animals.
claims.note: Read from the hop-classification test, which starts sign-in chains from the animals-dashboard endpoint.

claims.statement: The frontends redirect with absolute, browser-visible localhost addresses when run locally.
Journey forms carry hidden fields, such as the crumb, that a browser posts back with the answers.
claims.quote: Builds the fields a browser would post: the page's hidden fields, then the answers.

claims.statement: The animals journey's requests are tagged with these endpoint names: animals-origin, animals-commodities (and -search), animals-consignment-details, animals-identification, animals-import-reason, animals-additional-details, animals-documents (-upload, -status), animals-addresses with animals-party-picker (and -search), animals-cph-number, animals-port-of-entry, animals-transit-countries (-add), animals-transporters, animals-contact, each page with a -save.

The pages every journey shares are tagged animals-dashboard, animals-dashboard-search, animals-create, animals-hub, animals-notification-view, animals-declaration, animals-declaration-save, animals-amend, animals-cancel-amend and animals-cancel-amend-save, and the backend calls animals-backend-fulfilments, animals-backend-list and animals-backend-replace.
The journey signs in as the stub identity with CRN 2100010101.
claims.note: The stub password default in the same file is [REDACTED] and not copied.

claims.statement: The performance suite drives the journey frontends, among other services, over HTTP.
claims.quote: | Outbound | The services under test (INS frontend, journey frontends, reference-data, dynamics-gateway, stub, defra-id-stub) | HTTP | The traffic a suite generates |

claims.statement: The suite has no germinal-products journey: no set base, steps or endpoints for germinal products exist anywhere under src/, so no germinal route is exercised.
claims.ref: src/config/smoke.js:36-53 (JOURNEYS has only live-animals and high-risk-plants); grep -rli germinal src/ finds nothing

claims.statement: The suite asserts no page heading, caption, label copy or error message on any live-animals page; its only text check is that the dashboard search page contains the reference number.
The suite never shows a validation error path: it only posts answers that pass, so no live-animals validation rule or error message is exercised.
